title: Sore throat and fever
transcript:
Doctor: Hi, I'm Dr. Patel. What brings you in today?
Patient: My throat's been killing me for three days. It hurts to swallow.
Doctor: Any fever?
Patient: Yeah, 38.6 last night. No cough though.
Doctor: Are you taking any medications at the moment?
Patient: No, nothing.
Doctor: Any allergies to medications?
Patient: Penicillin. I got hives as a kid.
Doctor: OK. Your temperature today is 38.4. Your tonsils are swollen with white patches, and the lymph nodes in your neck are tender. The rapid strep test came back positive, so this is strep throat. Normally I'd give amoxicillin, but with your penicillin allergy we'll use azithromycin instead: 500 mg on day one, then 250 mg once a day for four more days.
Patient: Can I go to work?
Doctor: Stay home until you've been on the antibiotic for at least 24 hours and the fever is gone. Take paracetamol for the pain. If you can't swallow liquids or have trouble breathing, come back right away. Otherwise, come back only if you're not better in a week.
